title: Understanding the binding mechanisms of Alzheimer risk factor TREM2 in lipid bilayer using multi-scale molecular dynamics simulations
authors: Zhiwen Zhong; Martin Ulmschneider; Christian D. Lorenz
one_liner_zh: 该文用多尺度MD模拟研究TREM2/DAP12跨膜复合物在脂膜中的结合机制，属蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA互作，方法可迁移但对象不匹配。
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a widespread neurodegenerative condition affecting millions globally. Recent research has implicated variants of the triggering receptor ex-pressed in myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) as risk factors for AD. TREM2, an immunomodula-tory receptor on microglial surfaces, plays a pivotal role in regulating microglial activa-tion by associating with DNAX-activation protein 12 (DAP12). Despite its significance, the mechanism underlying the formation of the complex between the transmembrane domains (TMDs) of TREM2 and DAP12 remains unclear. This study employs multi-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate three TMD complex models, including two derived from experiments and one generated by AlphaFold2. Conducted within a lipid membrane consisting of an 80:20 mixture of phosphatidylcholine (POPC) and cholesterol, our analysis reveals hydrogen bonding interactions between K26 of TREM2 and D16 of DAP12 in all three models, consistent with previous experimen-tal findings. Our results elucidate the different spatial conformations observed in the models and offer insights into the structure of the TREM2/DAP12 TMD complex. Furthermore, we elucidate the role of charged residues in the assembly structure of the complex within the lipid membrane. These findings enhance our understanding of the molecular mechanism governing TREM2/DAP12 complex formation, providing a foundation for designing novel therapeutic strategies to address AD and other neu-rodegenerative diseases. Graphical Abstract Highlights Different TREM2/DAP12 complexes are generated using experimental PDB structures or AlphaFold2 Long time coarse-grained MD simulations are used for getting the sys-tems stable Atomistic detailed complex structures are captured using all-atom sim-ulation Provides mechanistic insight into TREM2 transformation from its un-bound state to bounded state Offers novel insights into the molecular basis of TREM2/DAP12 sig-nalling pathway
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer’s disease, AD）是一种影响全球数百万人的广泛性神经退行性疾病。近期研究已将髓系细胞触发受体2（triggering receptor expressed in myeloid cells 2, TREM2）的变异体视为AD的风险因素。TREM2，一种位于小胶质细胞表面的免疫调节受体，通过与DNAX激活蛋白12（DNAX-activation protein 12, DAP12）结合，在调节小胶质细胞活化中发挥关键作用。尽管其重要性，TREM2与DAP12跨膜结构域（transmembrane domains, TMDs）之间复合物形成的机制仍不清楚。本研究采用多尺度分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟，探讨了三种TMD复合物模型，其中两种源自实验，一种由AlphaFold2生成。在由80:20比例的磷脂酰胆碱（phosphatidylcholine, POPC）和胆固醇组成的脂质膜中进行，我们的分析揭示了所有三种模型中TREM2的K26与DAP12的D16之间的氢键相互作用，这与先前的实验发现一致。我们的结果阐明了模型中观察到的不同空间构象，并为TREM2/DAP12 TMD复合物的结构提供了见解。此外，我们阐明了带电残基在脂质膜内复合物组装结构中的作用。这些发现增进了我们对调控TREM2/DAP12复合物形成的分子机制的理解，为设计针对AD及其他神经退行性疾病的新型治疗策略奠定了基础。图形摘要亮点：使用实验PDB结构或AlphaFold2生成不同的TREM2/DAP12复合物；采用长时间粗粒化分子动力学模拟以获得系统稳定性；通过全原子模拟捕捉原子级详细的复合物结构；提供对TREM2从非结合态到结合态转变的机制性见解；为TREM2/DAP12信号通路的分子基础提供新见解。
